pinyin: jīng tiān dì qì guǐ shén
literal: shake · heaven · earth · make weep · ghosts · spirits
natural: moving heaven and earth and making the spirits weep

meaning.en: So stirring and powerful that it astonishes the world and even moves the spirits; used of heroic deeds or great art.
meaning.zh: 形容事迹或作品壮烈感人，震撼天地，连鬼神也为之哭泣。

examples.zh: 这部史诗描写了惊天地泣鬼神的英雄壮举。
examples.en: This epic describes heroic deeds that stir heaven and earth.

examples.zh: 他们在地震中的救援行动堪称惊天地泣鬼神。
examples.en: Their rescue work during the earthquake was truly awe-inspiring.

usage.en: Used attributively or predicatively for heroic deeds, tragedies and great works; often written with a comma, 惊天地，泣鬼神.
usage.zh: 多作定语、谓语，形容壮举、悲剧或杰作；也写作“惊天地，泣鬼神”。

natural: a Mongolian doctor

meaning.en: A derogatory colloquial term for an unqualified or incompetent doctor; a quack.
meaning.zh: 旧时对医术不高明或乱开药方的医生的贬称。

examples.zh: 别去找那个蒙古大夫看病，他连感冒都治不好。
examples.en: Don't see that quack; he can't even cure a cold.

examples.zh: 他自嘲说自己不过是个蒙古大夫，只会开点常用药。
examples.en: He joked that he was no more than a quack who could only prescribe common medicines.

usage.en: Colloquial and derogatory, often used jokingly or self-deprecatingly. The name is a historical stereotype and can sound offensive to some; avoid it in formal writing.
usage.zh: 口语，贬义，常带调侃或自嘲；正式场合避免使用。

natural: streets of flowers and lanes of willows

meaning.en: The red-light district of old times; places of entertainment and prostitution.
meaning.zh: 旧指妓院聚集的地方。

examples.zh: 小说里的公子哥儿常常流连于花街柳巷。
examples.en: The young gentlemen in the novel often loiter in the pleasure quarters.

examples.zh: 他年轻时出入花街柳巷，把家产都败光了。
examples.en: In his youth he frequented the red-light district and squandered the family fortune.

usage.en: Mostly seen in historical or literary contexts. Note 花柳 alone can also refer to venereal disease.
usage.zh: 多见于历史或文学语境。

natural: green towers and Chu halls

meaning.en: Brothels and entertainment houses of old China.
meaning.zh: 旧指妓院。

examples.zh: 这部电视剧里有不少青楼楚馆的场景。
examples.en: This TV drama has many scenes set in brothels.

examples.zh: 他常年混迹于青楼楚馆，早已声名狼藉。
examples.en: He has long hung around brothels and has a bad reputation.

usage.en: Literary term for the world of courtesans in historical settings. 青楼 originally meant a fine, painted building.
usage.zh: 文学用语，多用于历史背景；青楼本指华丽的楼房。

natural: supple as a swimming dragon

meaning.en: Describes graceful, powerful and flexible movement, such as dancing, martial arts or calligraphy.
meaning.zh: 形容身姿或笔势矫健灵活，像游动的龙一样。

equivalents: graceful as a dragon in flight

examples.zh: 他练剑时身形矫若游龙，让观众连连叫好。
examples.en: His body moved like a dragon as he practised the sword, and the audience cheered.

examples.zh: 这幅草书笔势矫若游龙，气势非凡。
examples.en: The brushwork of this cursive script is dragon-like and full of spirit.

usage.en: Often paired with 翩若惊鸿. Cao Zhi's 洛神赋 has 翩若惊鸿，婉若游龙, and 矫若游龙 is a variant of 婉若游龙. Used as predicate or in a comparison about movement.
usage.zh: 常与“翩若惊鸿”连用，作谓语，形容动作或笔势。

natural: heroic spirit that reaches the clouds

meaning.en: To be full of bold, heroic spirit that soars to the sky.
meaning.zh: 形容气概豪迈，直冲云霄。

examples.zh: 他举杯一饮而尽，豪气干云。
examples.en: He drained his cup in one go, brimming with heroic spirit.

examples.zh: 这首词写得豪气干云，读来令人振奋。
examples.en: This poem is full of heroic spirit and stirring to read.

usage.en: Used as predicate or attributive about a person's bearing or a piece of writing.
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语，形容人的气概或文章气势。

natural: a small token of my heart

meaning.en: To express one's feelings in a small way, usually through a modest gift.
meaning.zh: 略微表达一点心意，多用于送小礼物时。

equivalents: a small token of my appreciation
as a humble expression of my thanks

examples.zh: 这点土特产不成敬意，聊表寸心。
examples.en: This local produce is nothing much, just a small token of my gratitude.

examples.zh: 请收下这份薄礼，聊表寸心。
examples.en: Please accept this modest gift as a token of my regard.

usage.en: A polite phrase said when giving a gift; modest in tone, used in speech and letters.
usage.zh: 送礼时的客套话，谦虚委婉，口语和书信中都可用。

natural: cite the past to prove the present

meaning.en: To quote examples from history or the classics to support a view about the present.
meaning.zh: 引用古代的事例或典籍来证明今天的道理。

equivalents: draw on the past to make a point

examples.zh: 他在演讲中援古证今，说服力很强。
examples.en: He drew on history in his speech, which made it very persuasive.

examples.zh: 这篇论文援古证今，论述颇为充分。
examples.en: This paper cites the past to support its argument quite thoroughly.

usage.en: Used as predicate, mostly in writing about argumentation or scholarship.
usage.zh: 多作谓语，常用于论说或学术文章。

natural: crying for dad and shouting for mum

meaning.en: To wail and cry out in pain or panic.
meaning.zh: 形容因疼痛或惊慌而大声哭叫。

examples.zh: 孩子摔了一跤，哭爹喊娘地叫了半天。
examples.en: The child fell and wailed for ages.

examples.zh: 一听说要打针，他就哭爹喊娘。
examples.en: As soon as he heard he would get an injection, he started howling.

usage.en: Colloquial, often teasing or mocking. Used as predicate or adverbial.
usage.zh: 口语，常带调侃或嘲笑，作谓语或状语。

natural: three matchmakers and six betrothal rites

meaning.en: The full traditional procedure for a proper marriage; a formal, proper marriage.
meaning.zh: 旧指婚姻手续完备、礼数周全的正式婚娶。

equivalents: a proper wedding with all the trimmings

examples.zh: 老人希望孙子能三媒六聘，风风光光地把新娘娶进门。
examples.en: The old man hoped his grandson would marry in the full traditional manner.

examples.zh: 她说她要的不是三媒六聘，而是一份真心。
examples.en: She said what she wanted was not a full set of formal rites but sincerity.

usage.en: Usually describes a formal, respectable marriage, often alongside 明媒正娶. The numbers are symbolic.
usage.zh: 多指正式的婚娶，常与“明媒正娶”并用；数字为泛指。

natural: defy the edict and not obey

meaning.en: To disobey an imperial decree; to openly defy an order from above.
meaning.zh: 违抗皇帝的命令，不肯遵从。

examples.zh: 戏里的将军抗旨不遵，最终被削去官职。
examples.en: In the opera the general defied the edict and was finally stripped of office.

examples.zh: 在古代，抗旨不遵可是死罪。
examples.en: In ancient times, defying an imperial edict was a capital offence.

usage.en: Mostly used in historical settings or jokingly of defying an instruction. Opposite of 钦此钦遵.
usage.zh: 多用于历史语境，也可戏指不服从命令；与“钦此钦遵”相对。

natural: seeing an object brings sorrow

meaning.en: To feel sad on seeing an object that reminds one of a lost person or past time.
meaning.zh: 看到旧物就触动情怀，感到伤感。

examples.zh: 她看着亡夫留下的手表，睹物伤情。
examples.en: She looked at the watch her late husband left behind and was overcome with sorrow.

examples.zh: 搬家时翻出儿时的玩具，他不免睹物伤情。
examples.en: Finding his childhood toys while moving, he couldn't help feeling wistful.

usage.en: Used as predicate; typically about nostalgia or grief. Often followed by 思人.
usage.zh: 作谓语，多表怀旧或哀思，常接“思人”。

natural: standing like a mountain and still as a deep pool

meaning.en: Describes a person of great dignity and composure, as steady as a mountain and as deep as a pool.
meaning.zh: 形容人庄重沉稳，像山岳一样屹立，像深潭一样平静。

examples.zh: 老先生坐在那里，岳峙渊渟，一言不发便令全场肃然。
examples.en: The old gentleman sat there, imposing and composed, and his silence alone hushed the room.

examples.zh: 他为人岳峙渊渟，遇事从不慌乱。
examples.en: He is dignified and deep, never flustered by events.

usage.en: Literary praise of a person's bearing; also found as 渊渟岳峙 and 川渟岳峙, and also applied to calligraphy.
usage.zh: 文学性褒扬，形容人的气度；也可形容书法。

natural: drums and horns sounding together

meaning.en: Drums and bugles sounding at once, describing the clamour of a battle or a grand military scene.
meaning.zh: 战鼓和号角一起响起，形容战场上的喧闹声势。

examples.zh: 城下鼓角齐鸣，大战一触即发。
examples.en: Drums and horns sounded below the city, and battle was about to begin.

examples.zh: 影片开头便是鼓角齐鸣的战争场面。
examples.en: The film opens with a war scene of blaring drums and bugles.

usage.en: Used as predicate or attributive in descriptions of battle; occasionally of lively celebrations.
usage.zh: 作谓语或定语，描写战场气氛，偶尔也形容热闹的场面。

natural: leave some mercy under the mouth

meaning.en: To refrain from speaking harshly; to be gentle in what one says about others.
meaning.zh: 说话留有余地，不说得太刻薄。

examples.zh: 他已经很难过了，你就口下留情吧。
examples.en: He is already upset enough, so please go easy on him.

examples.zh: 批评同事时要口下留情，别伤了和气。
examples.en: When criticising colleagues, spare their feelings and don't harm the relationship.

usage.en: Usually used as a request or advice, e.g. 请口下留情. Often paired with 手下留情, which is a separate expression about restraint in actions.
usage.zh: 多用于请求或劝告，常与“手下留情”并用。

pinyin: rén bù rén guǐ bù guǐ
literal: person · not · person · ghost · not · ghost
natural: neither human nor ghost

meaning.en: Looking so wretched or strange that one hardly seems like a person; in a sorry state.
meaning.zh: 形容样子狼狈难看，或处境凄惨，不成样子。

equivalents: a shadow of one's former self

examples.zh: 病了一年，他被折磨得人不人鬼不鬼。
examples.en: After a year of illness, he had been reduced to a wreck.

examples.zh: 熬了三天夜，他一副人不人鬼不鬼的样子。
examples.en: After three sleepless nights he looked a complete mess.

usage.en: Colloquial and harsh; used as predicate or complement. Also stated 不人不鬼.
usage.zh: 口语，语气较重，作谓语或补语；也说“不人不鬼”。

natural: smiling with the skin but not the flesh

meaning.en: To smile on the surface without any real warmth; a forced or insincere smile.
meaning.zh: 脸上勉强装出笑容，内心并不高兴，含虚伪、不真诚之意。

equivalents: smile with one's teeth but not one's eyes

examples.zh: 他见了我皮笑肉不笑地点了点头。
examples.en: He nodded at me with a smile that didn't reach his eyes.

examples.zh: 别看她皮笑肉不笑的，心里不知道在盘算什么。
examples.en: Though she smiles without warmth, who knows what she is scheming.

usage.en: Used as predicate or adverbial; implies insincerity or hidden hostility.
usage.zh: 作谓语或状语，暗含虚伪或不怀好意。

natural: capable of the task and happy in it

meaning.en: To be fully competent for a task and carry it out with ease and satisfaction.
meaning.zh: 能力完全适合所担任的工作，做起来轻松愉快。

examples.zh: 这份工作他做得胜任愉快。
examples.en: He handles this job competently and happily.

examples.zh: 招聘要求写明：应聘者须能胜任愉快。
examples.en: The job advert states that applicants must be able to do the work with ease.

usage.en: Common in job descriptions, appraisals and recommendations; usually as predicate with 感到 or complement.
usage.zh: 常见于招聘、评语和推荐信，多作谓语。

natural: civil affairs as the warp and military as the weft

meaning.en: To have both administrative and military talents; to govern the state through both civil and military means.
meaning.zh: 文武兼备，既能治国安邦又能带兵打仗。

equivalents: a statesman and general in one
equally able in letters and arms

examples.zh: 诸葛亮文经武纬，辅佐刘备三分天下。
examples.en: Zhuge Liang, master of both civil and military affairs, helped Liu Bei carve out a third of the realm.

examples.zh: 他自诩文经武纬，实则一事无成。
examples.en: He claims to excel in both civil and military matters, but in fact has achieved nothing.

usage.en: Literary praise of statesmen and generals, used attributively or as predicate.
usage.zh: 文学性褒扬，形容政治家、将领，作定语或谓语。

natural: an angry look all over the face

meaning.en: A face full of anger.
meaning.zh: 脸上全是愤怒的神色。

examples.zh: 他怒容满面地冲进办公室。
examples.en: He burst into the office with a face full of fury.

examples.zh: 老板看完报表，怒容满面，一句话也没说。
examples.en: After reading the report the boss looked thunderous and said nothing.

usage.en: Used as predicate or adverbial in narration; the opposite of hiding one's feelings.
usage.zh: 多作谓语或状语，用于叙述。

pinyin: xǐ nù bù xíng yú sè
literal: joy · anger · not · show · in · face
natural: joy and anger do not show on the face

meaning.en: To keep one's emotions hidden and never show them in one's expression; to be composed and inscrutable.
meaning.zh: 喜怒等情绪不表现在脸上，形容人沉着、有城府。

equivalents: wear one's heart close to one's chest

examples.zh: 谈判桌上，他喜怒不形于色，让对手摸不透底牌。
examples.en: At the negotiating table he kept a poker face, leaving his opponents unable to read his hand.

examples.zh: 真正成熟的人往往喜怒不形于色。
examples.en: Truly mature people often don't let their feelings show.

story.en: The Records of the Three Kingdoms describes Liu Bei as a man of few words who humbled himself before others and never let joy or anger show on his face (喜怒不形于色).
story.zh: 《三国志》记载刘备“语言少，善下人，喜怒不形于色”。

date.zh: 西晋 · 约3世纪末（陈寿撰）
date.en: Western Jin, late 3rd c. (by Chen Shou)

usage.en: Usually praise for composure or political shrewdness, though it can also hint at secretiveness.
usage.zh: 多用来称赞沉着、有城府，有时也含难以捉摸的意味。

natural: sorrowful bowels broken inch by inch

meaning.en: Heartbroken; so sad that one's innards feel cut to pieces.
meaning.zh: 形容极度悲伤，好像肝肠一寸寸断裂。

examples.zh: 听到噩耗，她愁肠寸断，泣不成声。
examples.en: On hearing the terrible news she was heartbroken and sobbed uncontrollably.

examples.zh: 远行的儿子杳无音讯，母亲日夜愁肠寸断。
examples.en: With her travelling son silent, the mother was heartbroken day and night.

usage.en: Literary; used as predicate. Similar to 肝肠寸断 but focusing on worry and sorrow.
usage.zh: 文学性较强，作谓语；与“肝肠寸断”相近。

natural: climb up and cultivate the noble

meaning.en: To curry favour with the powerful and well-born in order to get ahead.
meaning.zh: 巴结有权势、地位高的人，以求抬高自己。

examples.zh: 他整天攀高结贵，想靠关系谋个好职位。
examples.en: He spends all his time sucking up to the powerful, hoping to land a good post through connections.

examples.zh: 她从不攀高结贵，凭本事吃饭。
examples.en: She never courts the powerful and earns her living on merit.

usage.en: Derogatory; used as predicate. Often compared with 攀龙附凤.
usage.zh: 贬义，作谓语；与“攀龙附凤”相近。
